topic: What happens to your lunch after you swallow it

sources.title: Your Digestive System & How It Works
sources.publisher: U.S. National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)

claims.text: Mouth to anus, the GI tract is about nine metres (30 ft) long.
claims.quote: covering a distance of about nine metres (30 ft); If you could stretch it out, it would measure 30 feet (9 meters)

claims.text: A ring-like muscle, the lower esophageal sphincter, relaxes to let food into the stomach.
claims.quote: a ringlike muscle—called the lower esophageal sphincter —relaxes and lets food pass into your stomach

claims.text: After four or five hours the stomach has emptied.
claims.quote: After four or five hours the stomach has emptied

claims.text: The small intestine, about 22 feet, is the longest part of the tract.
claims.quote: This 22-foot-long muscular tube is the longest part of your gastrointestinal tract; The small intestine is the longest part of the GI tract

claims.text: Transit through the small intestine averages about 4 hours.
claims.quote: Transit time through the small intestine is an average of 4 hours

claims.text: The large intestine absorbs water and the waste becomes stool.
claims.quote: Your large intestine absorbs water, and the waste products of digestion become stool

claims.text: Bacteria in the large intestine also break down food.
claims.quote: Bacteria in the large intestine can also break down food
